steps.title: Four downs to go 10
steps.body: A team on offense has four plays (downs) to gain 10 yards. If it does, it earns a new first down and the count resets. If not, the ball goes to the other team, usually after a punt on 4th down.

steps.title: Reading the situation
steps.body: Football describes situations as 'down and distance': '3rd and 4' means third down with 4 yards still needed. Every strategic choice in the sport starts here.

steps.prompt: It is 2nd down and 6. The offense runs for 2 yards. What is the next situation?
steps.explanation: The 2-yard gain leaves 4 yards still to go, and the next play is 3rd down.

steps.prompt: It is 3rd and 7. The offense gains 9 yards. What happens?
steps.explanation: Gaining the 7 (or more) yards needed earns a first down.

steps.statement: An incomplete forward pass keeps the clock running.
steps.explanation: The clock stops on an incomplete pass. It also stops when a runner goes out of bounds, on timeouts, and on most penalties.

steps.prompt: 4th and 20 from your own 22, down 3, 8:00 left. What is the right call?

options.why: Twenty yards is far too many. Punting protects field position and you still have time to get the ball back.
Your odds of 20 yards are tiny, and failing gives the opponent a short field.
You are about 80 yards from the posts; not an option.

steps.explanation: Long-distance 4th downs in your own territory are almost always punts.

steps.prompt: 4th and goal at the 1, down 4, 30 seconds left, one timeout. What is the right call?

options.text: Run or pass for the touchdown
options.why: A field goal would still leave you down 1. You need the touchdown, so you go for it.
A field goal makes it 3, which is still a one-point loss.
You are at the goal line; there is nothing to punt for.

steps.explanation: When a field goal cannot win the game, only a touchdown helps. Always compare the score to what each option is worth.

steps.prompt: How many downs does an NFL offense get to gain 10 yards?
steps.explanation: Four downs. Most teams punt or kick on 4th down instead of risking it.

steps.title: Stopping the clock
steps.body: The game clock stops on incomplete passes, when a ball carrier goes out of bounds, on timeouts (three per half), at the two-minute warning in each half, and for most penalties. It runs after in-bounds tackles, and a first down alone does not stop it.

steps.title: The play clock
steps.body: The offense must snap the ball within 40 seconds of the previous play ending (25 after some stoppages). If not, it is a delay of game penalty.

steps.title: Common penalties
steps.body: False start (offense moves early) is 5 yards. Offside (defense across the line early) is 5. Offensive holding is 10. Defensive holding is 5 plus an automatic first down. Facemask and roughing the passer are 15. An official throws a yellow flag to mark a foul.

steps.prompt: Match each penalty to its yardage.
steps.explanation: Know these four and most flags make sense instantly.

steps.prompt: A defender holds a receiver during a pass play. What happens?
choices: 5 yards and an automatic first down
steps.explanation: Defensive holding is 5 yards plus an automatic first down, which is why it is so costly.

choices: An automatic timeout at 2:00 of each half
steps.explanation: It is at the two-minute mark of the 2nd and 4th quarters.
Offensive holding is 10 yards. False start and offside are the 5-yard fouls.

steps.prompt: The offense takes more than 40 seconds to snap the ball. What is the penalty?
steps.explanation: Delay of game is a 5-yard penalty.

steps.prompt: After a normal play ends, how long does the offense have to snap the ball?
steps.explanation: 40 seconds from the end of the previous play, 25 after some stoppages. Run out and it's delay of game.

steps.prompt: An offensive lineman flinches before the snap. What is the call?
steps.explanation: A set offensive player who moves before the snap commits a false start: 5 yards, and the play never starts.

steps.prompt: A pass bounces off the turf before the receiver secures it. What is it?
choices: Incomplete: the down is used and the ball goes back
A fumble the defense can recover
A catch, if he holds on after
steps.explanation: A pass that hits the ground is incomplete: the down is used, the ball returns to the previous spot, and the clock stops.

steps.prompt: Who throws the yellow flag when a foul happens?
steps.explanation: Officials throw yellow flags for fouls. A coach's red flag is a challenge, not a foul.
